title: form metadata type: define, register and serve `form` items (ADR-0159, card ②)
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYpEsWWE9Y5YtSsDgqZ

Source: ADR-0159 (PR #36957), decisions D1 to D6 and D8, and its five ruled merge questions. Parent: #36868, card ② of five. Maintainer ruling 2026-11-24, record 7123091354 on #36444: 「拆成 form 类型，对外表单并入」. The five merge questions are ruled (ruling record 7131569242 on #36868, 2026-11-24: 「表单拆成独立 form 元数据类型的 5 个合并问题 都同意」, all option A); questions 1, 3, 4 and 5 are requirements of this card, marked below. They are decided: ⛔ none is re-opened here.

Parent card #36868 (the ADR step) is done: ADR-0159 merged in PR #36957.
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
(Seat note: the `(narrowing)` arm is fixed by `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the changeset gate reads `narrowed` beside a line without it as a contradiction, and the arm brings the title's `!` and the dogfood battery. The seat confirms the `yes` at claim; `yes` is expected: a new metadata type, new exports, and item 7's new error code, which is always `yes`.)

Grading: `area:build` · Feature · adds the `form` metadata type and serves it · builders and administrators who author or publish forms · evidence: ADR-0159's readings at `main` `62692b7f8b`. p1 by the blocker rule (#36444 waits on card ③, which waits on this).

## What to build

One releasable change. Nothing an author wrote stops loading, and `view` reads behave as before. Old-shape writes save as before with one exception (item 5): a package-less `view` write that would store a list at a name a read-only package authors as a `form` item is refused, and some of those saves are admitted today. That is why the card is `narrowed` and not `added` (a value refused is `narrowed`; several kinds take `narrowed` over `added`).

1. **The type** (ADR-0159 D2, D3). A `FormSchema` in `packages/spec/src/ui/`, derived by reference from `FormViewSchema`: `name` (qualified `OBJECT.KEY`, the part before the last segment must equal `object`), `object` (required), `label` (optional), the form body at the top level (ruled question 5: no `config` wrapper), plus `protection`, the ADR-0010 fields and the ADR-0146 `overrides` declaration. No `viewKind`, `config`, `isDefault`, `order` or `scope`. `data` is refused by name with the prescription to bind with `object`. `object` must name an object the package can reference, judged where a view's object is judged today (`os validate`, publish) (D2).
2. **Registration, in one change**: the `MetadataTypeSchema` member, the `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` row (`page`'s flags; file patterns `**/*.form.ts|yml|json`; the suffix is free once item 3's rename has moved the Studio modules off it), the metadata-core lockstep enum, the type-to-schema map, the stack collection `forms` with its plural and singular map entries, and `form: listed` in `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` (the pin in `customization-package.test.ts` fails without it). The showcase's `KIND_COVERAGE` row with one authored `form` item: a new public form on an address no other form holds (`examples/app-crm` and `examples/app-showcase` both publish `/forms/contact-us` today; take another). ⛔ No action targets it and no existing form is moved: the console reads forms from `view` until card ③ (#37087), so an action-opened `form` item would answer not found.
   - **Hand-keyed per-type arms outside the registry.** List in the PR every arm keyed on `'view'` under `packages/rest/src`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src` and `packages/spec/src/kernel` (`git grep -nE "=== 'view'|'view'," -- packages/rest/src packages/metadata-protocol/src packages/spec/src/kernel`), and for each say whether `form` takes an arm and why. Read at `254e396a29e`: the per-caller read gate, its packaged-base map and its translate arm in `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`; `META_COMPILE_CACHE_TYPES` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/meta-compile-cache.ts`; `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-create-seeds.ts`; `packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts`. A caller who is refused a form's document at `/api/v1/meta/view/NAME` today is refused it at `/api/v1/meta/form/NAME`.
3. **The factory** (ruled question 1 = A). `defineForm` becomes this type's factory and the existing Studio schema-bound metadata-form helper is renamed `defineMetadataForm`, both in this card, as a declared compiler-carried export break.
   - **Scope of the rename, counted from the tree** (ADR-0159 question 1, "For the cards"; at `689e5695b98` `git grep -lw defineForm` names 60 files, 41 of them code). Count again at your own head and put the count in the PR:
     - 17 `*.form.ts` modules under `packages/spec/src` that import and call it;
     - 3 that declare, export or build around it: `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/index.ts`, and `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts`, whose pure-constructor set names it (the renamed helper joins that set);
     - 4 tests: 3 under `packages/spec` that call it, 1 under `packages/lint` that names it in a test title;
     - 17 that name it only in a comment: 10 tests (9 under `packages/spec` and `packages/lint`, 1 under `ui/`) and 7 sources (3 under `packages/lint/src`, 2 under `packages/spec/src/system`, `packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts`, `scripts/i18n-bundle-surface.mjs`);
     - 19 that are not code: 6 generated outputs to regenerate (the `packages/spec` API-surface and export-origin snapshots, the generated reference page), 9 released or historical texts ⛔ not edited (seven `CHANGELOG.md`, a released notes page, an audit), and 4 hand-written (two `packages/spec/liveness/` files, one internal skill under `.claude/`, this ADR). The `.claude/` file is a governed path: leave it out of this PR and name it in the report for the seat.
   - **The file suffix moves with the name** (ADR-0159 D2; the owning seat's routing on question 1, seat record 7132202077 on PR #36957, not the ruling's own words). The `form` type takes `*.form.ts`. The 17 Studio modules are renamed `*.metadata-form.ts`, and `METADATA_FORM_MODULE_SUFFIX` in `scripts/i18n-bundle-surface.mjs` becomes `.metadata-form.ts`. Readers of the suffix, measured at `689e5695b98` (count again at your head):
     - the one matcher, `scripts/i18n-bundle-surface.mjs` (constant and predicate), and the files that spell the suffix beside it: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.self-test.mjs` on nine lines across several cases (5641 to 5691, and 5881), one of which asserts `endsWith('.form.ts')` on the live walk (line 5662) and so fails as soon as the modules are renamed; the kind text in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs`; a fixture path in `scripts/pm/landing-k.mjs`; the comments of `scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs` (lines 163 to 170). `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` names a temporary fixture file `skill.form.ts` and reads no suffix. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (Tier H) imports the predicate and spells no suffix: ⛔ do not edit it; if your head shows it must change, stop and report;
     - import specifiers: 31 files under `packages/spec/src` import a `.form` module (the seven domain barrels, `system/metadata-form-registry.ts`, 23 tests). Thirty spell it `./NAME.form`; `packages/spec/src/kernel/repeater-item-titles.test.ts` imports 15 modules as `../DIR/NAME.form`. Sweep by both spellings;
     - **text that teaches the suffix: re-word it, do not re-point it.** Once `*.form.ts` is the new type's suffix, "a `*.form.ts` module binds `data`" teaches the wrong root for an app's `lead.form.ts`. Name the Studio modules by their new suffix in: the `data` root explanation in `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`; the `data` arm of the message in `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (it spells `*.form`); the docblock wording of `packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts` together with the two `toContain` pins on it in `validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts`, and a third string pin in the same test file, on the emitted text: the tokens the explanation of the mislayered-root rule must print (the `MOVED` table lists `*.form.ts` for `VISIBILITY_ROOT_MISLAYERED`, line 1904 at `be1c0cbd4da`), which changes with the explanation in `rule-explanations.ts`; and the row "Metadata-editing forms (`*.form.ts`)" in `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`;
     - generated outputs that print the module paths (`packages/spec/export-origins/`): regenerate, never hand-edit;
     - path citations in ledgers, checklists and comments (`packages/spec/liveness/`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/`, comments under `packages/lint/src`, `packages/cli/src`, `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/`): re-point the ones that name a live file; released text (a `CHANGELOG.md`, a released changeset, a migration entry of a past major) is not rewritten;
     - prove the rename with the i18n bundles: `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write` changes no bundle value, and `pnpm check:i18n` is green.
   - **First step, before any edit**: read the seat's outside-use reading on this card (a comment that carries the output of `gh search code defineForm --owner objectstack-ai` and the head of each repository read). If the card carries none, take the reading yourself the same way and record the tree and commit of each repository in the PR. "Outside use" is any import or call of `defineForm` from `@objectstack/spec` outside `objectstack-ai/objectstack`. The ruling rests on that use being platform-internal.
   - **If outside use is found (one hit is enough): stop and report `needs_decision`.** The fallback is a new factory name, ⛔ never a dual-meaning overload, and by the ruling it returns to the maintainer for a word before it is built. It is not the dev's or the seat's to take.
4. **The projection** (D5): one pure function beside `expandViewContainer` that turns a `view` body into the `form` items it carries (the container's `form`, each `formViews` entry, a `viewKind: 'form'` item), under the name each is served as today, an item's `config` lifted to the top level (ruled question 5). It is the only reader of the old shapes for form content: loader, stored-row read, doors, withdrawal judgement and lint all call it.
   - **A projected item is served as the form is served today.** It takes `object` from today's four-rung resolution (`anonymousFormObjectName`) and its body unchanged (D5). ⛔ The authored-only refusals of item 1 (`data` by name; the name's prefix equals `object`) are not applied to a projected item: the view item never enforced that equality (D3), and nothing an author wrote stops loading. Rule 7's "cannot be read" (item 6) is a body the projection cannot turn into items at all, ⛔ never an item that fails an authored-`form` refusal.
5. **Reads and writes of `form`**: authored items plus projected ones, a projected item marked in its read envelope; an authored item shadows a projected one of the same name in the same package, inside one layer (a package's source item over the projection of its own source; a stored `form` row over the projection of a stored row at the same address), and ⛔ a package's source item never shadows the projection of a stored row; a `form` save, reset or delete at `(package, name)` also removes the old-shape row carrying that form at that address, in the same transaction (an item-shaped `view` row deleted, a stored container re-saved without the form). ⛔ It removes form content only: a list item of type `view` that holds the same `OBJECT.KEY` name is left untouched.
   - **A stored old-shape row keeps replacing its base's form when the base moves to `form`** (ADR-0159 D5, D6 rule 11). The overlay merge runs inside one type today (`mergePackageAwareOverlay`), and a package may move its source to `forms:` while a stored `view` row still stands over the form (card ④ does that to first-party apps). So the effective `form` read resolves a package's form over both types in the one served-row order (`servedOverlayRowCandidates`): the stored `view` row that order picks at the package's address — the pair's declared override, a row bound to the package, a package-less row, a stored container whose expansion writes the name — is served, as the `form` item it projects, over the package's source `form` item of that name. A stored `form` row at the same place in the order wins over the stored `view` row.
   - **A declared `form` override is admitted where the base ships the form in either type** (ADR-0159 D4, D7-b). `judgeOverrideWrite` asks "does the base ship this item" inside one type today and refuses `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`). For `form` it reads the base's forms through the projection as well, so a `form` override of a base that still authors an old shape saves. Card ③'s Setup switch and designer write exactly this row, and until card ④ every first-party form is an old shape: without this read a public form of an installed app cannot be switched off from Setup. A `form` override of a name the base ships in neither type is still refused.
   - **A stored `view` row that carries no form at a form's name is read as written over the form only in three bindings** (ADR-0159 D5): two are closed by a write door that exists today, the third by a refusal this card adds. A list and a form of one name are two items (D3), so a list row closes nothing by sharing a form's name. Nothing is served for the name from the package only where the row is: a declared override of the package (the override write gate refuses a declaration of an item its base does not ship in that type, `declared_package_ships_no_such_item`); a row bound to a read-only package (once the package ships the name as a `form` item, a `view` save naming the package there is a new item in a read-only package and is refused, `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`); or a package-less row, an item or a stored container whose expansion writes the name. ⛔ A list saved in a package beside the form (an app of the environment's own, or the base's pair as the pair's own item with no `overrides`) is never read this way, as an item or as a container's expansion: the form stays served. A row in a writable package is that package's own item, and a read-only package's own `views:` container that expands a list at the name of its own `form` item is its list beside its form.
   - **For the served `form` read the projection reads served rows only** (ADR-0159 D5). A stored `view` row enters the effective `form` read through the projection only where the served-row order serves that row today; a row the order passes over is projected into no served read (it stays in whichever withdrawal layer reads it today, where it may only narrow). ⛔ Do not project every stored `view` row. **"Served" is asked at each package's address**, inside the `form` read's own resolution over both types, and ⛔ never taken from the effective `view` list: one row can be the served row at one package's address and be passed over at another's (a package-less row is in every package's order). Once a read-only package authors its form in `forms:` it has left the `view` type, so the `view` merge no longer resolves its address; a package-less row that stands over its form is still the served body there, whatever a writable package holds at the name. The case it decides: a package-less `view` row that carries an open form, behind a writable package's own `view` row that carries a list of the same name, is read by no layer today and both doors answer `404`; they answer `404` after this card too.
   - **Add one refusal, kept as long as rule 11's replacement check is kept (card ⑤ does not remove it): every package-less `view` write that would store a list at a name a read-only package authors as a `form` item** (in `forms:`; a form the projection reads out of a package's old shape does not trigger it). No door of today closes it: ADR-0146 D11's close (`packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal`) refuses only where its ceremony would move the row (it stays open for a name several packages ship, a base whose pair cannot be formed or ensured, a container body, a row whose pair already holds the item), and the container name-collision refusal in `protocol-save.ts` judges names shipped as `view` items. ⛔ Do not build it by extending the D11 close: it must not ask the state of the base's pair or how many packages ship the name. It covers a save, the publish of a draft, and a rollback to a version that carries a list at the name (a delete is not judged: it stores nothing), of an item and of a container whose expansion writes the name (judge the expansion as the readers place it, as the container name-collision refusal does), and a re-save of a row already stored (the stored row keeps its bytes). It sits beside the container name-collision refusal and answers with its envelope (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `400`); no new error code. The message names the form and the two saves that work whether or not the base has a pair: another key, or the list saved into an app of the environment's own. ⛔ It never prescribes a save under a name another stored row holds. A package-less `view` write that carries a form at the name is an old-shape write of the form and saves as before. **It refuses saves that are admitted today**, where the package's form is still an old-shape `view` item: several read-only packages ship the name; the base has no pair that can be formed or ensured; a re-save of a stored row whose pair already holds the item; a container that overlays the package's own container by its own name. Name these and the door that remains in the changeset.
   - **Known limit, fail-closed**: a package-less row that carries a list at the name and was stored before this refusal judged the write (before the package shipped anything under the name, or through a corner today's doors leave open) is read the same way, an item and a container's expansion alike (today's answer inside one type). The form's layered read names the row that stands over it.
   - **Measure first**: does any write door admit a declared override whose body carries no form at a name its base ships as a form (a list item saved over a form's name)? Record the reading in the PR with the tree and commit, and report it either way. The disposition at major 19 of a row that carries no form over a linked base is ruled (ruling record 7136809727 on #36868 (「两类特殊的旧存储行怎么处置。不考虑」)): it gets none of its own and stays as stored. The measurement says only whether the declared row can exist. If a door admits it, the closed-reading pin below gains that row as a second fixture in this change.
6. **The anonymous doors and the withdrawal judgement over both types** (D6, rules 1 to 9 and 11): candidates from the effective `form` read, resolved over both types as item 5 says, so a stored row that closes an address by replacing its base's body keeps closing it; the withdrawal layer is the effective lists and the per-package layers of both `form` and `view`, old shapes passed through the projection first; narrowing only, in both directions; identity is the served name and, inside one name, the whole item, so a same-name withdrawal closes the form whatever slug either side declares, and a definition under another name is a different form (rule 6: the slug match decides no case in this layer); a stored body the projection cannot read closes the links it names and says so once at `error`, naming the row (type, name, package), the links it closed, and the way out that exists in this release: an old-shape save that repairs the body. ⛔ The message names no command that does not ship; the ceremony card (⑤a) adds the ceremony's name to it. `404 FORM_NOT_FOUND` for a switched-off form is unchanged. The tenancy intake advisory and the organization-scoped refusal judge `form` writes too.
   - **The reader of old-shape withdrawals is exempt from ADR-0087's kit age-out** (ruled question 4 = A, D6 rule 10, D7; a permission boundary). Build the read of a withdrawal in a stored old-shape body as its own named function inside the two-type layer, and mark the exemption where it lives: ADR-0159's id and the words "exempt from the ADR-0087 age-out; leaves only by a release whose upgrade precheck refuses a deployment still holding an old-shape form row" in its docblock, and its own anchor file in `scripts/adr-anchors/`. ⛔ It is not registered as an ADR-0087 conversion-layer entry, so no retirement clock starts on it. No withdrawn public form may re-open. The precheck itself is card ⑤'s (major 19).
7. **The public address clash** (ruled question 3 = A). The `form` write door, `os validate` and publish each refuse a `form` whose open slug another form already holds, naming both forms. It is a refusal on the new type only: an old-shape `view` write keeps today's first-match behaviour, and nothing an author has today narrows. "Another form" is judged over the effective `form` read, so a projected old-shape form holding the slug counts. A form holds an address while its `sharing.publicLink` names it, switched on or off (ADR-0159 question 3, "What holds means"): a switched-off form that keeps its link still holds it. The refusal is judged at every `form` save that leaves the form open, Setup's switch included. That reading is the record's own, marked outside the ruled block. It refuses one arrangement that is served today: a retired form that keeps its link, switched off, beside its successor open on the same address. The doors keep serving what is stored; the successor's next `form` save and `os validate` are refused, naming both, until the retired form's link is cleared. A new error code goes through the ledger (`check:error-code-casing`).
8. **Translations** (D8): the `forms` family in the bundle schema, the extractor and the translation lint; the translator reads `forms.NAME` first and the form tails under `objects.OBJECT._views.KEY` as the declared fallback; section copy keeps `objects.OBJECT._sections.SECTION` as its object-level default. `label` and `description` under `_views.KEY` are not form tails: they are neither moved nor read as a fallback (ADR-0159 D8).
9. **Lint**: the form walkers read `form` items and the projection; the consumer-less warning of D1 (successor of `form-view-internal-not-loaded`). ⛔ It is not raised for an item that declares `overrides` when the base's form of that name has a consumer: an override with no link over a linked form is what keeps that address closed, and a warning that it steers nothing would invite its removal. ⛔ No new warning, notice or deprecation for an old shape in this card: `form-view-internal-not-loaded` stays as it is and is the only advisory on the old shapes (D5).
10. Leave the ADR id in the code, and anchor the doors' two-type read and the exempt withdrawal reader in `scripts/adr-anchors/` (one file per anchor).

## Done when

- A stack with `forms: [...]` loads, serves `GET /api/v1/meta/form` and `/api/v1/meta/form/NAME`, and publishes; `os validate` refuses a name whose prefix differs from `object`, an authored `data` key, and a taken public address; the metadata save door and publish refuse the taken address too. Each of the three refusals has a pin asserting status and `code` and naming both forms, one pin shows an old-shape `view` write on a taken slug still saves as before, and one pin shows a `form` saved open on the address of a switched-off form is refused (ablate: the switched-off half of the holder read).
- A `form` save, a reset and a delete at a name a list item of type `view` holds each leave the list row byte-equal (ADR-0159 D5; ablate: the form-content test of the old-shape row removal).
- A `form` save, a reset and a delete at `(package, name)` each remove the old-shape row that carries that form, in the same transaction: an item-shaped `view` row is gone; a stored container is re-saved without the member, its lists byte-equal; a `form` write that fails leaves both rows as they were.
- The override gate over both types (item 5): a `form` override saved through the save door into the pair of a base whose form is an old-shape `view` item is admitted; a `form` override of a name the base ships in neither type is refused `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` (ablate: the projection half of the gate's "ships" read; the first save is refused).
- The projection serves what is served today (item 4): an old-shape form whose `data.object` differs from its container's object answers on both doors as before this change, byte-equal on the resolve door (ablate: parse projected items with `FormSchema`; the form is closed or dropped).
- Rule 9: in an organization-scoped environment a `form` save that would leave a withdrawn form open is refused as the same `view` save is today, with the withdrawal held in the other type (status and `code`; ablate: the `form` arm of the write-time judgement).
- The address clash never refuses a save that leaves the form closed: switching off either form of a clashing pair saves (ablate: judge the clash on every `form` save).
- Translations (item 8): `forms.NAME.title` wins over `objects.OBJECT._views.KEY.title`; the tail is read when the family has no value; `objects.OBJECT._views.KEY.label` is not read for a form; the extractor emits no `_views` tail for an authored `form` item.
- The consumer-less warning (item 9): raised for an item with no link that no action targets; not raised for an item that declares `overrides` over a base form that has a consumer; no new advisory is raised for an old shape.
- The per-type arm inventory of item 2 is in the PR, with one pin: a caller refused a form's document at `/api/v1/meta/view/NAME` is refused it at `/api/v1/meta/form/NAME`.
- The row that carries no form at a form's name (ADR-0159 D5), two pins, each with an ablation:
  - the bound: over a package that authors an open `form` item, a list saved package-less at the form's name is refused (status `400`, `code` `VALIDATION_ERROR`), a package-less container whose expansion writes a list at that name is refused, and both are refused where the base's pair cannot be ensured; the same list saved into an app of the environment's own, and into the pair as its own item, saves; after all of them the two doors serve the package's form at its address (ablate: the bound, by letting the reading take any stored `view` row of the name; the doors answer `404`. Ablate: the expansion half of the refusal; the container saves and the doors answer `404`);
  - the closed reading: a package-less `view` row that carries a list at the name, seeded as stored, keeps both doors at `404` at the package's address, and so does a stored package-less container whose expansion writes a list there (ablate: fall through to the package's source `form` item when the stored row projects no form).
- Served rows only (ADR-0159 D5), one pin with an ablation: a writable package's own `view` row that carries a list, and a package-less `view` row of the same name that carries an open form; both doors answer `404` at the form's address before this card's change and after it (ablate: project every stored `view` row into the `form` read; the address answers). A second fixture, for the address: a read-only package authors an open `form` item, and a package-less `view` row of that name whose form has no link stands over it; a list of the name is then saved into an app of the environment's own, and into the pair as its own item; both doors answer `404` at the package's address before the list is saved and after it (ablate: take the served rows from the effective `view` list; the address answers).
- A stack that still authors the three old shapes loads unchanged, and each of its forms is also served as a `form` item under the same name. `GET /api/v1/meta/view` answers exactly what it answered before (pin against a fixture taken before the change).
- The public form of `examples/app-crm` answers at its address before and after, byte-equal on the resolve door.
- The eight D6 pins exist, each asserting status, `code` and that no record was written, each with one ablation run recorded in the PR (rebuild, on-disk mutation proof, restore proved by an empty `git diff HEAD`):
  - withdrawn by a `view` override in `.custom`, open as an authored `form` of the same name (ablate: the `view` half of the layer);
  - the mirror (withdrawn by a `form` override, open as an old-shape item in the base); the withdrawing row is written through the save door, not seeded (ablate: the `form` half of the layer);
  - withdrawn in a container's `formViews` entry, open as a `form` item named for the expansion (ablate: the projection step of the layer);
  - withdrawn in a body of the same name whose link names another slug than the open definition's: both doors answer `404` at the open definition's address (ablate: the whole-item match of rule 6, by making it require an equal slug);
  - a per-package-layer withdrawal in either type (ablate: `getMetaItemsPerPackage` for that type);
  - an unreadable old-shape body closes its links, and the boot error names the row, the links and the repair save (ablate: rule 7);
  - replacement across the types (rule 11): a stored `view` override in `.custom` whose body has no `publicLink`, over a base that authors the same name as an open `form` item, and its twin with a package-less row: both doors answer `404` at the base's address (ablate: the cross-type resolution of item 5, by serving the package's source `form` item when the stored row is a `view` row);
  - the submit door refuses wherever the resolve door does.
